title: Auto-Scaling Strategies
description: Learn how auto-scaling adjusts capacity based on demand, explore reactive and predictive policies, and avoid common scaling pitfalls.

data.text: Auto-scaling automatically adjusts the number of active servers or resources based on current demand. Instead of manually provisioning servers during peak hours, auto-scaling keeps costs low while maintaining performance during traffic spikes.
Reactive scaling responds to real-time signals such as CPU utilization, request latency, or queue depth. When a metric crosses a configured threshold, the system adds or removes instances.

items: Simple to configure and widely supported in cloud platforms
Responds to actual load after the threshold is breached
May react too late during sudden spikes if scale-up time is long
Risk of scale oscillations if thresholds are too aggressive
Does not account for scheduled traffic patterns

data.title: Pro Tip
data.text: Add cooldown periods between scaling actions to prevent rapid scale oscillations that waste money and destabilize the cluster.
Predictive scaling uses historical data and machine learning to forecast demand. Instead of waiting for load to spike, it pre-provisions capacity in anticipation of known patterns.

items: Greatly reduces cold-start latency for predictable workloads
Learns from seasonal or daily traffic patterns automatically
Requires enough historical data to make accurate predictions
May over-provision if predictions are inaccurate
Often combined with reactive scaling as a safety net

data.caption: Auto-scaling loop with load balancer and metric source
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    Client --> LB[Load Balancer]
    LB --> ASG[Auto Scaling Group]
    ASG --> Inst1[Instance 1]
    ASG --> Inst2[Instance 2]
    ASG --> InstN[Instance N]
    Inst1 & Inst2 & InstN -->|metrics| CloudWatch[CloudWatch / Metrics]
    CloudWatch -->|scale signal| ASG
    ASG -->|add/remove| Instances[(Instance Pool)]
    Instances --> Inst1 & Inst2 & InstN

rows: Keep metric at target value (e.g., 60% CPU)
Scale by defined steps per threshold breach
Can over-scale if steps are large
Scale by fixed amount after a wait period

items.text: Set scale-up thresholds slightly ahead of saturation
items.hint: Don't wait for 100% CPU before scaling.

items.text: Ensure instance launch time is fast enough to handle expected spikes
items.hint: Use pre-warmed or containerized workloads when possible.

items.text: Define a minimum instance count to avoid full outages
Use health checks so unhealthy instances are replaced automatically

data.text: Auto-scaling only works well when your architecture supports it. Stateless services, container orchestration, and fast image-based deployments make auto-scaling effective. Stateful services require careful data placement and warm-up strategies before new instances can safely join the cluster.
